# Computed `is<Ntype>` flags are undocumented and invisible to search

## Context

`Neo.setupClass()` synthesizes an `is<Ntype>` boolean onto every class prototype, walking the whole ntype chain — **229** of them (see the census below). Only **three** are read anywhere, and they are load-bearing: `grid/Container.mjs:536` infers TreeGrid mode from `store.isTreeStore`, and TreeGrid's ARIA emission depends on the result.

The flag names never appear as literals anywhere. They are computed from a string at class-creation time, so `grep isTreeStore src/` returns exactly one hit: **the read site**. That reads like a textbook dangling reference — a consumer with no producer — and the behaviour is documented in no guide.

This is not hypothetical. On 2026-08-31 a maintainer (me) broadcast a defect-note to `AGENT:*` claiming *"TreeGrid mode can never activate — `grid/Container.mjs:536` reads an `isTreeStore` flag no class defines, so `isTreeGrid` is permanently false"*. That claim was false and has been retracted. The static grep was the only evidence, and the grep is structurally incapable of seeing the producer.

## The Problem

The synthesis is undocumented in `learn/`. Measured:

| probe | hits in `learn/` |
|---|---|
| `is<Ntype>`, `is${`, `ntypeChain`, `ntype chain`, `prototype flag`, `capitalize(Neo.camel` | **0** |
| **positive control** — files mentioning `ntype` at all | **40** |

The control fires, so this is an absence rather than a search artifact.

The consequence generalises past one flag: **any of the 229 synthesized flags** can be "grepped into" a false defect the same way, because the instrument and the mechanism are mismatched by construction. It does **not** generalise to every `is[A-Z]…` property — most are ordinary configs or state, and conflating the two is itself a mistake this ticket made and corrected (below).

**Corrected census (2026-08-31).** This ticket originally cited `.isDestroyed` (105), `.isLeaf` (40), `.isRecord` (39) and `.isConstructed` (25) as examples. **That was wrong** — @neo-gpt caught it in review of PR #17905. None of those four is ntype-derived: `isLeaf_` is a reactive config, `isConstructed` is `core.Base` state, `Neo.isRecord` is a utility, and `isDestroyed` is lifecycle state. The read counts were true; the *cause* attached to them was invented.

Measured properly — deriving each flag with the real `Neo.camel`/`Neo.capitalize` rather than a reimplementation, which itself mis-produced one name:

| quantity | instrument | value |
|---|---|---|
| `ntype:` string occurrences anywhere in `src/` | textual scan — **WRONG INSTRUMENT** | 234 |
| …of which are instance/layout configs that never reach `setupClass` | `hbox`, `vbox`, `card`, `flexbox`, `my-functional-component` | 5 |
| **class-level own `ntype` in a `static config`** | **acorn AST parse, 0 parse failures** | **229** |
| `is<Ntype>` flags therefore synthesized | one per declared `ntype` | **229** |
| of those, flags with at least one reader | grep for `.is<Flag>` | **3** |

**The first correction used the wrong instrument too.** A textual `ntype:` scan counts *instance* configs — a layout `{ntype: 'card'}` or an `items` entry — which never enter `setupClass` and synthesize nothing. Only a class's **own `ntype` in its `static config`** does. @neo-gpt caught this on the re-review; it is the third instrument/population mismatch in this ticket's own history, which is precisely the failure the ticket documents.

*Cross-checked and settled:* @neo-gpt initially measured 228, then retracted it — his fresh Babel **and** independent Acorn passes both yield **229** with zero parse failures, matching my Acorn walk. Three parses, two authors, one figure.

The three real readers are `isBasefield` (`src/form/Container.mjs:414`), `isContainer` (`src/worker/App.mjs:583`) and `isTreeStore` (`src/grid/Container.mjs:536`) — a set both @neo-gpt and I reproduce independently. The trap is unchanged in kind: any synthesized flag can be grepped into a false conclusion.

A subtler failure runs the other direction: because the flag is derived from `ntype`, **renaming an `ntype` silently renames every flag derived from it**, and no static search will surface the readers that just went `undefined`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/Neo.mjs:849` — `setupClass(cls)`.
- `src/Neo.mjs:1026-1028` — the synthesis, over the full chain, so subclasses inherit every ancestor's flag:

```js
// Add is<Ntype> flags to the prototype
ntypeChain.forEach(ntype => {
    proto[`is${Neo.capitalize(Neo.camel(ntype))}`] = true
});
```

Derivation, executed rather than reasoned — `ntype: 'tree-store'` → `Neo.camel` → `'treeStore'` → `Neo.capitalize` → `'TreeStore'` → `proto.isTreeStore = true`. Runtime check with a negative control:

```
TreeStore.prototype.isTreeStore : true
TreeStore.prototype.isStore     : true       (inherited via the ntype chain)
Store.prototype.isTreeStore     : undefined  (negative control — fires)
```

- `learn/guides/coreengine/SetupClass.md` is the **authority**: `learn/tree.json` registers it as the class-compilation guide, and it is what the Knowledge Base ranks first for `setupClass` questions. Its *"What Does `setupClass` Do?"* inventory omitted type-flag synthesis entirely, so the KB answered that the flags come from trailing-underscore reactive configs.
- `learn/guides/fundamentals/ExtendingNeoClasses.md` §5 is a **neighbouring** surface, not the authority. It opens *"the engine performs **several crucial operations**"* and then documents exactly one, so it earns a concise linked echo.
- `learn/Glossary.md:140-143` defines `ntype` purely as a configuration alias, with no mention that it also derives a prototype predicate.

Incidental: `ExtendingNeoClasses.md` has two `## 5.` headings (lines 174 and 201).

## The Fix

Documentation only — no runtime change. The behaviour is correct; only its discoverability is missing.

1. **`learn/guides/coreengine/SetupClass.md`** — the **authority**. It is the guide `learn/tree.json` registers for class compilation, and the one the Knowledge Base ranks first for `setupClass` questions, yet its "What Does `setupClass` Do?" inventory omitted type-flag synthesis entirely. A new section 3 documents the derivation, the chain-walk, the real readers, and — because this is the observed failure mode — how it differs from section 2's trailing-underscore reactive API.
2. **`ExtendingNeoClasses.md` §5** — a concise echo linking the authority section. Not the detailed home: it is a neighbouring fundamentals guide, not the registered class-compilation surface.
3. **`learn/Glossary.md`** — the `ntype` entry records the derived flag and links the authority **section**.
4. Renumber the duplicate `## 5.` heading in `ExtendingNeoClasses.md`.

**Why the authority moved (correction, 2026-08-31).** The first version put the detailed explanation in `ExtendingNeoClasses.md` and claimed it documented the fact "once, where it happens". @neo-gpt demonstrated observable harm rather than a taxonomy preference: he asked the Knowledge Base how `setupClass` generates `is<Ntype>`, it ranked `SetupClass.md` first, and it answered — incorrectly — that the flags come from trailing-underscore reactive configs. Documenting the neighbour left the canonical lookup still wrong.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — documents existing behavior; no ADR authority is created, amended or challenged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `learn/guides/coreengine/SetupClass.md` documents the `is<Ntype>` synthesis as a numbered `setupClass` operation: derivation from `ntype`, chain-walk semantics, a worked example naming a real class, and an explicit contrast with the trailing-underscore reactive API.
- [ ] `ExtendingNeoClasses.md` §5 carries a concise echo that links the authority section rather than restating it.
- [ ] The guide states explicitly that these property names are **computed** and therefore invisible to static search, and that one grep hit at a read site is not evidence of a dangling reference.
- [ ] The guide notes that renaming an `ntype` renames its derived flags, with no static signal at the read sites.
- [ ] `learn/Glossary.md`'s `ntype` entry records the derived flag and links the authority **section anchor**, not a guide root.
- [ ] The duplicate `## 5.` heading in `ExtendingNeoClasses.md` is renumbered.
- [ ] Any flag census in the ticket, PR or docs names **only** measured ntype-derived flags, with the derivation computed via `Neo.camel`/`Neo.capitalize` rather than a reimplementation.
- [ ] Verification: each documented claim is reproducible from `src/Neo.mjs` — the doc cites `setupClass` rather than restating the algorithm from memory.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to the synthesis itself, or to `grid/Container.mjs:536` — both are correct as written.
- Adding redundant `@member {Boolean} isX=true` JSDoc to individual classes. That scales with class count and would drift; the mechanism is documented once, where it happens.
- A lint or guard that resolves `is<Ntype>` reads against the ntype chain. Possibly worthwhile later; it is not what this ticket buys.

## Avoided Traps

- **Documenting it only at the read site** (`grid/Container.mjs`) — would help exactly one flag of the whole synthesized population and leave the general trap intact.
- **Treating the incident as the subject.** The gap predates the false defect-note and would remain if that note had never been sent; the incident is evidence, not the problem.
- **"Just grep harder."** No grep spelling finds a name assembled from a string at runtime. The fix has to be documentation, not technique.
